transcript.text: Good morning everyone. We've got eighteen totes of spent solvent from the cleaning process staged in the waste area, and they're awaiting disposition. I need to get a shipment plan together and sign off on it, but per our policy, we need to review the current waste classification and transport arrangements during our routine waste-disposition huddle before I can authorize anything. Has anyone started looking into the classification or coordinated with our recycling contractor yet?

transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we go any further. My laboratory review this morning classified the solvent as UN1993 flammable liquid, packing group II — not as routine recyclable solvent. This means the 18 totes must be transferred into 18 UN-rated steel drums before shipment, and a hazardous-waste manifest is required. The classification isn't in the formal waste register yet because I'm waiting for the plant manager's disposition signature.

transcript.text: I've been in contact with the licensed hazardous-waste carrier, and they'll accept these 18 drums only for a Friday 16:00 pickup, provided they're arranged on exactly 3 pallets and the manifest is submitted by 12:00 Friday. I held off on booking the pickup because the waste classification was still awaiting confirmation — which Jonas just provided.
